security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown formatting or read-only command examples and are false positives. The supplied Bash implementation genuinely collects local Git, Jira, Obsidian, and calendar data, writes it to a predictable temporary file, and sends context to an AI CLI. Users should review data permissions and the draft before any publication.

remediation.issue: The sample workflow aggregates potentially sensitive work, ticket, vault, and calendar data for an AI CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval for every source, minimize fields, redact secrets and personal data, and document the AI service data policy before submission.

remediation.issue: The sample workflow uses the predictable path /tmp/standup-context.json.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp with restrictive permissions, avoid shared temporary storage where possible, and remove the file with a cleanup trap after processing.

remediation.issue: The workflow can post a generated draft to Slack.
remediation.suggestion: Keep posting opt-in, display the final destination and content for review, and never automate publication without explicit user confirmation.

content.value_statement: Remote teams often need updates from scattered work records. This skill turns approved project context into a concise standup draft for human review.
actual_capabilities: Organizes standup drafts into Yesterday, Today, and Blockers sections.
Explains how to summarize recent Git commits into accomplishments.
Provides Jira query examples for completed and in-progress work.
Provides guidance for using recent Obsidian notes and calendar events as context.
Suggests concise formatting for Slack, email, Discord, or Obsidian.
Includes examples for identifying dependencies and escalation needs.
limitations: It does not validate the accuracy or completeness of connected data sources.
It requires configured integrations for Git, Jira, Obsidian, and calendar data.
Generated drafts need human review before sharing with a team.
The sample automation may handle confidential project and personal information.

use_cases.title: Prepare a daily engineering update
use_cases.description: Turn recent commits and assigned tickets into a short draft for a daily async standup.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a distributed team
use_cases.description: Create consistent updates that highlight priorities, meetings, dependencies, and requests for help.

use_cases.title: Document project progress
use_cases.description: Use a repeatable note structure to summarize completed tasks and next steps across project records.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a simple standup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise standup draft from these accomplishments, today priorities, and blockers. Use Yesterday, Today, and Blockers headers.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize recent commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize these recent commit messages into three outcome-focused standup bullets. Preserve ticket references and avoid technical detail that does not help the team.

prompt_templates.title: Combine approved sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Using only this approved Git, Jira, note, and calendar context, create a standup draft. Flag uncertain links between commits and tickets instead of guessing.

prompt_templates.title: Review a standup for publication
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this standup draft for accuracy, sensitive information, unclear ownership, and missing blockers. Return recommended edits before I share it.

output_examples.input: Completed API authentication, fixed a queue retry issue, and have a database migration planned today.
output: Yesterday: Completed API authentication and resolved the queue retry issue.
Today: Finish and test the database migration.

output_examples.input: Waiting for database replica access and reviewing JIRA-234 today.
output: Yesterday: Investigated the migration validation approach.
Today: Review JIRA-234 and prepare migration tests.
Blockers: Waiting for read-only database replica access from the database team.

best_practices: Confirm which data sources are approved before collecting context.
Use outcome-focused bullets and include clear ownership for blockers.
Review drafts for accuracy and sensitive information before posting.
anti_patterns: Do not publish generated updates without human review.
Do not include secrets, private customer data, or unnecessary personal details.
Do not infer ticket status or completion from incomplete context.

faq.question: What information can this skill use?
faq.answer: It provides patterns for using approved Git commits, Jira tickets, Obsidian notes, and calendar events.

faq.question: Does it post messages automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides a sample workflow. Any posting should require explicit human review and confirmation.

faq.question: Can I use it without Jira?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance supports graceful fallback when Jira data is unavailable.

faq.question: Should I share all commit details?
faq.answer: No. Share only information needed for the update and remove sensitive details.

faq.question: Can it identify blockers?
faq.answer: It can help structure explicit blockers and highlight patterns that may need review.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The playbook includes guidance for Markdown-based updates such as Slack, Discord, email, and Obsidian notes.
